meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/2F, Friday 8 November 2024, P75159A). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded WITH mark_split. Every (Total for Question) line was recovered except q1–q5, each of which is a single mark; the paper sums to the printed 80.

coding_notes: q4 (name a polygon) tagged properties_of_2d_shapes, the node added 2026-09-04 precisely for this and for the two AQA rows that had been sitting on angles_in_polygons.

q13 (show a triangle is isosceles from a reflex angle and a straight line) tagged angles_on_lines_and_circles alone. The mark scheme's reasons are angles at a point, angles on a line and the triangle sum — all inside that one node — and the isosceles conclusion is stated, not derived from shape properties.
q15 (map scale to a real length in km) tagged ratio then converting_measurements, which is the ordering the coding doc names for map-scale items and files it under Ratio and Proportion.

q22 (better value across two currencies) tagged proportion, the documented handling for currency conversion. The mark scheme accepts routes through unit price, unit mass or quantity-per-unit-cost, all of which are that node.

q26 tagged areas_of_triangles FIRST although two of the five marks are forming and solving a linear equation and a third is Pythagoras. The question asks for an area and the accuracy mark is the area; the ordering is the documented forced choice, not a judgement about where the work is.
q28 tagged compound_units before volume_of_a_prism: the answer is a density, and the volume is the input to it.
q17b tagged reverse_percentage rather than percentage_change — a bonus of a known cash value is 5% of the unknown total, which is the reverse direction.
